text:
maria: FYI spotted a sudden drop in token-saved numbers on the runtime rollup dashboard, looks like cache key formation changed after yesterday's kernel tweak. linking panel: https://dash.redwood.local/d/prefetch/metric-explorer

jon: ugh. how big is the drop? new kernel changed batching path or kv layout?

maria: ~38% drop in week-over-week token-saved for model-recommended routes, per-model breakdown shows one model (open-7b-v2) took most of the hit. route slice /assistant/generate shows biggest variance.

leo: can you paste a sample of the kv key vs old key? might be a normalization mismatch (whitespace, punctuation) or different seq boundary.

maria: here's a couple examples from the profiler logs:
```
kv_key_old=seed:v1:open-7b-v2:/assistant/generate:prompt_hash:0x3f8a2e
kv_key_new=seed:v1:open-7b-v2:/assistant/generate:prompt_hash:0x3f8a2e:batcher-v2
hit=false
```

anya: looks like the new key adds a `:batcher-v2` suffix. that would fragment the keyspace and drop hit-rate unless we backfill normalization. did batching heuristics change tokenization boundaries?

maria: yes the batching change appended the execution path tag so we could route compatible kernels, forgot to mark it as non-key-affecting for prefix cache.

jon: that explains kernel selection influence — adding runtime metadata to the key is making semantically identical prompts miss. can we add a key-normalizer that strips known runtime-tags before hashing?

leo: quick experiment idea: generate normalized keys at read time and do a sample lookup against the old keyspace; produce hit-probability estimate. I can run a 1% traffic fork.

maria: please run it. I'll also spawn a dashboard slice for "normalized key hit simulation" and add per-customer delta column so we can see who loses the most tokens. example SQL for the simulation query: 
```
-- simulate normalized hits
with samples as (
  select ts, model, route, customer_id, prompt, raw_key,
         regexp_replace(raw_key, ':batcher-v2$', '') as normalized_key
  from prefetch.raw_keys
  where ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
  limit 200000
)
select model, route, customer_id,
       count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from prefetch.key_index ki where ki.key = samples.normalized_key)) as simulated_hits,
       count(*) as requests
from samples
group by model, route, customer_id
order by simulated_hits desc
limit 200;
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by @maria for runtime/batcher-v2 (id: dpl-2024-11-14-09). 

anya: also check TTL semantics — if new keys are never backfilled, short TTLs will prevent recovery via warmup. what do we see on warmup coverage?

maria: warmup coverage panel shows warmup hit-rate fell from 72% -> 44% for the affected routes. per-customer breakdown: mid-market customers with lots of short prompts lost the most.

jon: let's prioritize fix: (1) short-term: add normalizer on read path (non-destructive) + backfill job to write normalized key copies; (2) medium: change key generation to canonical form and roll kernel tag to metadata store; (3) long: add gating in rollout so key-shape changes are flagged by the key-sim test.

leo: I can own the backfill job. will run a dry-run against archived index first. ETA 6h for dry-run, 18h for live backfill if results align.

maria: thanks — I pushed a tiny patch that strips runtime tags in cache lookup. patch: `cache.lookup(normalize_key(k))`. can we test on canary?

deploy-bot: canary deploy dpl-2024-11-14-09 -> done (10% traffic).

anya: canary metrics look promising: normalized simulated_hits ~ +32% in the canary slice, overall token-saved is improving. I'll keep monitoring for regressions and kernel fallback errors.

jon: after backfill we should re-run profiling to confirm KV hotspots didn't regress (sha lookups, hashing CPU). add perf counters: `kv.hash_time_ms`, `kv.lookup_ms` to the warmup dashboards.

maria: added those counters. also created a lightweight runbook entry in #eng-runtime (pinned) for future batching-key changes. short-term rollout plan: full deploy once backfill completed and per-customer token-saved is within 5% of baseline.

leo: starting dry-run now, will post results.

maria: thanks team. will keep this thread updated with the backfill progress and final numbers. :pray:
